Is it true I cannot cook while I am on my period?
cases.truth: False. Menstrual blood is not dirty; you can cook and serve food normally.

cases.q: My aunt says I should not bathe during my period. Is she right?
cases.truth: False. Washing is good for you and warm water can ease cramps.

cases.q: Is it true girls should not play sport while menstruating?
cases.truth: False. Any physical activity is fine and exercise often reduces cramps.

cases.q: Does using a tampon mean I am no longer a virgin?
cases.truth: False. Virginity relates to sexual activity, not period products.

cases.q: Is period blood the dirty blood the body is getting rid of?
cases.truth: False. It is the lining of the uterus, made of tissue and blood.

cases.q: My friend says irregular periods mean something is seriously wrong.
cases.truth: Usually false, especially in the first two years.

cases.q: You cannot get pregnant during your period, right?
cases.truth: False. It is less likely but possible.

cases.q: If I miss a period it definitely means I am pregnant.
cases.truth: False. Stress, illness, weight change and early menstrual years can all delay a period.

cases.q: Should girls avoid talking about periods around boys?
cases.truth: False. Periods are a normal biological process and talking about them helps girls get support.

cases.q: My grandmother says putting herbs inside keeps you clean down there.
cases.truth: False and harmful. The vagina cleans itself; substances inside cause infection.

cases.q: Do you lose a dangerous amount of blood every period?
cases.truth: False. Most people lose 2 to 5 tablespoons across the whole period.

cases.q: Can washing my hair during my period make me sick?
cases.truth: False. Washing is good for you.

cases.q: Is it true that girls should stay home from school during their period?
cases.truth: False. You can attend school; support exists if pads or facilities are the problem.

cases.q: Someone told me a tampon can get lost inside your body.
cases.truth: Not supported by the corpus; the assistant should say what it does know or refer on rather than invent.

cases.q: Is it true you should only change your pad twice a day to make them last?
cases.truth: False. Change every 4 to 6 hours; leaving a pad too long risks infection.
